description: People with technical skills are welcome.
summary: FlameScope is an interactive, SI-powered web dashboard that turns 20 NASA PSI microgravity combustion investigations (BASS, Saffire, SAME, FLEX, ACME and more) into fire safety guidance for the ISS, the Artemis Moon Base, pressurized rovers, Mars habitats and spacesuits. Pick a destination in a live 3D scene and every investigation is re-ranked with a transparent relevance score based on oxygen, pressure, airflow, fuel type and fire safety directness. A scroll-driven oxygen chart and a draggable oxygen-pressure envelope reveal the critical gap: no solid-material microgravity data covers the 30-34% O2 atmospheres planned for the Moon. Each experiment can be re-flown as a live simulation that flags when you extrapolate beyond NASA's tested range, and a 3D Gravity Gap scene shows that no partial-gravity combustion data exists yet. Google Gemini, grounded in the curated dataset, writes cited crew briefings, interprets and compares experiments, and answers questions. Everything is tagged Prevention, Detection or Suppression, with Earth spinoffs linked to the data. It helps researchers and engineers find, compare and interpret fire data faster, so the next giant leap is a safer one.
details: WHAT IT DOES FlameScope is an interactive, SI-powered dashboard that summarizes, ranks and interprets 20 NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) combustion investigations to deliver fire safety insights for crewed exploration. It covers BASS and BASS-II, Saffire-I/II/III, SAME and SAME-R, DAFT and DAFT-2, FLEX, FLEX-2, CFI, the six ACME experiments (BRE, CFI-G, E-FIELD Flames, CLD Flame, Flame Design, s-Flame), SPICE and SLICE. HOW IT WORKS 1. 3D Mission Space: a real-time three.js scene with Earth, the ISS, the Moon with a lunar base and pressurized rover, and Mars with a habitat. Clicking a destination flies the camera there and sets the mission atmosphere (O2, pressure, airflow, gravity) for the whole app. 2. The Oxygen Ascent: a scroll-driven chart from 12% to 100% O2. Each row is the oxygen range one investigation actually tested; rows light up as you pass through them, exposing the data gap at the 30-34% O2 exploration atmospheres planned for the Moon Base and rovers. 3. Experiment Simulator: every investigation re-runs as a live simulation (flame spread over solids, droplet burning and cool flames, spherical burners, co-flow jets, smoke transport to detectors). Sliders show NASA's tested range and the app warns when you extrapolate beyond it. 4. Mission Control: a guided four-step flow. Choose a destination; check a draggable oxygen-pressure flammability envelope; see every investigation ranked by a transparent relevance score (O2 fit 30%, pressure 15%, airflow 10%, fuel relevance 15%, fire safety directness 30%) with a per-factor breakdown; then compare up to three investigations side by side (radar chart plus a table that flags shared hardware, fuels, sensors and variables) or ask the AI analyst. 5. Gravity Gap: an interactive 3D scene where a shader-driven flame morphs from a blue microgravity sphere to a yellow 1 g teardrop. It shows that PSI holds no partial-gravity combustion data, points to E-FIELD Flames as the only proxy, and names LUCI and FM2 as future data. 6. Investigation dossiers: objective, fuels, sample geometry, O2, pressure, airflow, diluents, sensors, what varied between tests, findings, Earth applications and a direct link to the dataset in NASA PSI. SI LAYER Google Gemini receives the complete structured dataset, the live ranking and auto-generated insights with every request. It writes cited crew fire safety briefings, interprets single experiments for a chosen atmosphere, explains similarities and differences between investigations, and answers free-form questions. Citations become clickable links to the source investigation, and the model is instructed not to invent numbers and to name the missing experiment when the data cannot answer. BENEFITS AND IMPACT Researchers and engineers can find the most relevant microgravity fire data for a given habitat in seconds, see exactly where data exists and where it does not, and get grounded interpretations. The key finding it surfaces: no solid-material microgravity test in PSI covers the oxygen-enriched, low-pressure atmospheres planned for the Moon, and no partial-gravity data exists at all. Every insight is organized by NASA's three pillars, Prevention, Detection and Suppression, and the Back on Earth section links the data to spinoffs such as water-mist extinguishers, smarter smoke detectors and firefighter gear. TOOLS Next.js 15, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, three.js with React Three Fiber, Framer Motion, Recharts, Lenis, Supabase (Postgres) for the dataset and anonymous question log, Google Gemini API for the SI layer, and Vercel for hosting. CREATIVITY AND CONSIDERATIONS FlameScope treats fire safety as a mission-planning question rather than a database search: you choose where the crew will live and the evidence reorganizes around them. We kept the scoring fully transparent, flagged condition ranges summarized from public descriptions as approximate, and made the AI cite every claim so it can be checked. Limitations: a curated subset of 20 investigations, heuristic simulations (not CFD), and relevance weights that should be validated with NASA fire safety researchers.
